# Competency Map — EM Interview Story Builder

This reference maps Engineering Manager competency areas to the interview questions they generate. Use it to:
1. Identify what competencies a story covers when scanning raw experience material
2. Present the full set of interview questions a story can answer
3. Spot non-obvious secondary uses for a story with a reframe

---

## People Management

**Core behaviours**: setting clear expectations, giving direct feedback, developing individuals, managing underperformance, having difficult conversations, running 1:1s, supporting career growth, building psychological safety.

**Interview questions this covers**:
- "Tell me about a time you had to manage underperformance in your team."
- "Describe a difficult conversation you've had with a team member."
- "How do you approach developing engineers who are early in their careers?"
- "Tell me about a time someone on your team wasn't meeting expectations. What did you do?"
- "How do you balance supporting someone while still holding them accountable?"
- "Give me an example of when you had to give feedback that was hard to deliver."
- "How do you build trust with a new team?"
- "Tell me about a time you had to let someone go, or put them on an improvement plan."

---

## Delivery & Execution

**Core behaviours**: owning delivery outcomes, improving predictability, removing blockers, managing risk, recovering struggling projects, scope management, running effective sprint/planning processes, balancing speed and quality.

**Interview questions this covers**:
- "Tell me about a time a project was at risk of missing its deadline. What did you do?"
- "How do you ensure your team delivers predictably?"
- "Describe a time you had to rescue a struggling team or project."
- "Tell me about a time when requirements kept changing. How did you manage it?"
- "How do you handle scope creep?"
- "Give me an example of how you've improved delivery processes."
- "Tell me about a time something went wrong with delivery. How did you respond?"
- "How do you prioritise when there's too much to do?"

---

## Technical Leadership

**Core behaviours**: setting and maintaining engineering standards, making architectural decisions, managing technical debt, driving code quality, CI/CD adoption, tooling decisions, working with senior ICs and architects, owning documentation and interfaces.

**Interview questions this covers**:
- "How do you approach setting engineering standards across a team?"
- "Tell me about a time you had to make a significant technical decision."
- "How do you manage technical debt while still delivering features?"
- "Give me an example of how you've improved code quality or engineering practices."
- "How do you handle it when a team resists adopting new standards or tooling?"
- "Tell me about a time you had to balance technical rigour with delivery pressure."
- "How do you stay technically credible as a manager while no longer writing code day-to-day?"
- "Describe your approach to documentation and knowledge management."

---

## Stakeholder Management

**Core behaviours**: managing expectations, influencing without authority, navigating conflict between teams, pushing back constructively, managing upwards, building cross-functional relationships, communicating bad news.

**Interview questions this covers**:
- "Tell me about a time you had to influence someone who had more authority than you."
- "Describe a situation where you had to push back on a stakeholder or senior leader."
- "Give me an example of a conflict between teams that you had to resolve."
- "How do you manage stakeholder expectations when things aren't going to plan?"
- "Tell me about a time you had to deliver difficult news to a stakeholder."
- "How do you build relationships with people outside your immediate team?"
- "Tell me about a time you disagreed with a decision made above you. How did you handle it?"
- "How do you handle it when two stakeholders want conflicting things?"

---

## Change & Innovation

**Core behaviours**: driving adoption of new tools, processes or ways of working; leading change in a resistant environment; influencing culture; running communities of practice or knowledge sharing; proposing and landing improvements.

**Interview questions this covers**:
- "Tell me about a time you drove change in a team or organisation."
- "How do you get buy-in for a new idea when people are resistant?"
- "Give me an example of a time you introduced a new tool, process, or practice."
- "Tell me about a time you had to change how a team worked. How did you bring them along?"
- "How do you foster a culture of continuous improvement?"
- "Describe a time you evangelised something new across a wider organisation."
- "How do you approach innovation in a risk-averse or compliance-heavy environment?"

---

## Conflict & Difficult Situations

**Core behaviours**: managing interpersonal conflict on a team, handling a difficult team member, navigating disagreements between senior engineers, de-escalating tension, working with difficult personalities.

**Interview questions this covers**:
- "Tell me about a time you had to deal with conflict within your team."
- "Describe a situation where a senior technical person was creating friction."
- "How do you handle it when two strong personalities clash?"
- "Tell me about a time a team member undermined trust or team cohesion."
- "Give me an example of a difficult working relationship you had to navigate."
- "How do you maintain team health when there's interpersonal tension?"

---

## Values & Character

**Core behaviours**: acting with integrity under pressure, making hard ethical calls, building inclusive environments, being accountable when things go wrong, showing resilience, demonstrating commitment.

**Interview questions this covers**:
- "Tell me about a time you had to make a decision that was right but difficult or costly."
- "Describe a situation where you had to uphold a principle under pressure."
- "How have you built an environment where everyone feels included and able to contribute?"
- "Tell me about a time you made a mistake as a manager. What did you do?"
- "How do you hold yourself accountable when something goes wrong on your watch?"
- "Tell me about a time you had to be resilient through a prolonged difficult period."
- "Give me an example of how you've demonstrated commitment to your team."

---

## Growth & Learning

**Core behaviours**: reflecting on and learning from failure, acting on feedback received, changing approach based on experience, growing as a leader.

**Interview questions this covers**:
- "Tell me about a time you failed as a manager. What did you learn?"
- "Describe feedback you received that changed how you work."
- "What would you do differently if you could go back and handle a situation again?"
- "How do you continue to develop yourself as a leader?"
- "Give me an example of a time you changed your mind or approach based on new information."

---

## Story → Competency Quick Reference

Use this to rapidly identify what a new story is likely to cover before drilling into detail.

| If the story involves... | Primary competency | Likely secondary |
|---|---|---|
| An individual not meeting expectations | People Management | Values (accountability), Delivery |
| A struggling or underdelivering team | Delivery & Execution | People Management, Technical Leadership |
| A process you introduced or improved | Change & Innovation | Delivery, Technical Leadership |
| Conflict with another person or team | Conflict & Difficult Situations | Stakeholder Management, Values |
| Persuading someone to adopt something new | Change & Innovation | Stakeholder Management |
| A technical decision under pressure | Technical Leadership | Delivery, Stakeholder Management |
| A difficult stakeholder or senior leader | Stakeholder Management | Values (integrity), Conflict |
| Requirements changing or scope growing | Delivery & Execution | Stakeholder Management |
| Taking accountability for something that went wrong | Values & Character | Delivery, People Management |
| Feedback you gave or received | People Management | Growth & Learning |
| Launching or scaling a community / practice | Change & Innovation | Technical Leadership |
| Introducing a mentoring or development programme | People Management | Change & Innovation |
